## Keep the datasets distinct

The School A categorical example describes a **hypothetical sample of 40 students**: Walk 8, Bicycle 6, Bus 18, and Car 8. The quantitative graph lessons use a **separate hypothetical sample of 24 one-way commute times**. Neither dataset is a record of actual Maple Hill School students. Changing the display never changes its observations.

<div data-chart="commute-dot" class="chart-frame"><p>Commute times: 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 42, 48, 58 minutes.</p></div>

## How to study with this book

Read an explanation, predict what will happen, and then use the activity. For construction questions, draw on paper before opening **Show solution**. A correct answer includes appropriate labels, a sensible scale, and reasoning in context—not only arithmetic.

The activities run in your browser without an account or notebook kernel. Choices are not submitted to a teacher and reset when you reload the page. Core explanations and worked answers remain readable without JavaScript. Printing expands solutions and includes activity reference states.

Existing chapter addresses remain available. The editable Unit 1 chapters, data, code, and tests are organized in the repository's **Unit 1** folder, with one subfolder per topic and a **Shared** folder for material reused across topics.
